audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven level-chart rows are inverted against their own why text. whys[0] says Renekton wins the raw level-1 all-in but win[0] is Gnar; whys[1] describes a free chunk and a shove but win[1] is Skill; whys[2] says the window is 'pure Rage timing' but win[2] is Renekton; whys[3] says 'Mega up flips the all-in' and whys[5] and whys[6] both describe Gnar pulling clear, yet all three rows read Renekton.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Renekton, Gnar, Skill, Gnar, Gnar, Gnar, Gnar], matches every why line, and matches the 53.17% win rate — the `late` paragraph even cites that number while the chart above it says he wins levels 3 onward.
audit.corrected: All six rows flipped as one atomic group in both layers; level 1 down to 4/10 for Renekton, Gnar rows 6-7/10, level 3 to 5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer phases were template text and gave no cooldowns, on a page whose whole instruction is 'trade around Ruthless Predator'.
audit.why: Ruthless Predator is 16s at rank 1 and only 8s at rank 5, and Cull the Meek is 7s flat — the shape of the lane is that his stun cooldown halves as the game goes on while your punish window shrinks with it.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[N].why rewritten to the real story, with the Fury threshold and the two stun durations moved into dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The empowered Ruthless Predator does two things the page never mentions: it DESTROYS damage shields on the target, and it stuns for 1.5 seconds instead of 0.75 — double duration. Separately, Cull the Meek heals him off every unit it hits, which is what makes his short trades win.
audit.why: All three are in Riot's own text, and both the shield-break and the heal are flagged in _missing for this exact pairing. The shield-break matters directly: a Gnar holding Sterak's Gage as the answer to his all-in loses that shield to the empowered W.
audit.corrected: Fury threshold, both stun durations and the shield destruction stated in dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[1].d; the heal and its anti-heal answer stated in dosFull[1].d.

edits.before: Boomerang + hop kite wins every melee matchup early. Identify how Renekton contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Renekton's point-click W stun and fury-empowered autos win the raw level-1 all-in against your squishy Mini body outright.

edits.before: Rage management is the champion — track your own bar. Only take the trade when Renekton's Ruthless Predator is down.
edits.after: Your level-2 Hyper third-hit plus a returning Boomerang is a free chunk his short-range stick cannot answer.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Renekton must walk into your range.
edits.after: Level 3 hinges on your Rage bar: with Mega you wall-combo a kill, without it his W stun-lock punishes Mini.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Ruthless Predator's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Mega up flips the all-in: bait his W and both Slice and Dice charges, then Wallop and GNAR! him into a wall with no dash left.

edits.before: Mega + R against a wall is the best engage top lane owns. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Renekton's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: His level 6 is just more fury while yours is the Mega wall-combo, so a loaded Gnar out-trades and kills at full Rage.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Ruthless Predator's cooldown.
edits.after: Your first-item Mini Boomerang poke out-paces his fading fury combos and chips him at no risk.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Renekton carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: He has no sustained threat past items, while your wall-GNAR! and kiting scale into an elite teamfighter late.

edits.before: Boomerang Renekton's last-hits, AA-hop out of his reach, and time Mega so the transform lands ON his engage window.
edits.after: Cull the Meek heals him off every minion, so buy Executioner's before you try to win a long trade at range.

edits.before: Renekton wastes Ruthless Predator (Stun) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Above 50 Fury his W stuns for 1.5 seconds instead of 0.75 and shreds shields.

edits.before: That is Renekton's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Read the fury bar: above 50 every ability of his gets a second, worse effect.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields outright.

notes: The shield-break on the empowered W is the finding worth carrying forward: report[8].t lists Sterak's Gage as a core item in a lane where his stun deletes damage shields on the target before the fight resolves. I did not rewrite the itemisation line because that is a build call, not a fact correction, but it deserves a look. Riot's E text says only that Renekton dashes; it does not mention two charges. The page's 'both Slice and Dice charges' framing is standard and Riot's text does not contradict it, so I left it and reused it rather than asserting a charge count of my own.
